description: Canonical method references available to manuscript citation selection. Use only when the corresponding method is present in evidence.

references.title: Generalized Gradient Approximation Made Simple
references.raw_reference: Perdew, J. P.; Burke, K.; Ernzerhof, M. Generalized Gradient Approximation Made Simple. Phys. Rev. Lett. 1996, 77, 3865.
references.citation_guidance: Use when the reported calculations actually use the PBE exchange-correlation functional.

references.title: Improved adsorption energetics within density-functional theory using revised Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof functionals
references.raw_reference: Hammer, B.; Hansen, L. B.; Nørskov, J. K. Improved adsorption energetics within density-functional theory using revised Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof functionals. Phys. Rev. B 1999, 59, 7413.
references.citation_guidance: Use when the reported calculations actually use RPBE or a revised PBE functional for adsorption energetics.

references.title: Efficient Iterative Schemes for Ab Initio Total-Energy Calculations Using a Plane-Wave Basis Set
references.raw_reference: Kresse, G.; Furthmüller, J. Efficient Iterative Schemes for Ab Initio Total-Energy Calculations Using a Plane-Wave Basis Set. Phys. Rev. B 1996, 54, 11169.
references.citation_guidance: Use when VASP is the electronic-structure code actually used; a generic plane-wave basis or cutoff alone is insufficient.

references.title: Projector Augmented-Wave Method
references.raw_reference: Blöchl, P. E. Projector Augmented-Wave Method. Phys. Rev. B 1994, 50, 17953.
references.citation_guidance: Use when the reported calculations actually use the PAW method.

references.title: A Consistent and Accurate Ab Initio Parametrization of Density Functional Dispersion Correction (DFT-D) for the 94 Elements H-Pu
references.raw_reference: Grimme, S.; Antony, J.; Ehrlich, S.; Krieg, H. A Consistent and Accurate Ab Initio Parametrization of Density Functional Dispersion Correction (DFT-D) for the 94 Elements H-Pu. J. Chem. Phys. 2010, 132, 154104.
references.citation_guidance: Use when the reported calculations actually apply the DFT-D3 dispersion correction.

references.title: Special Points for Brillouin-Zone Integrations
references.raw_reference: Monkhorst, H. J.; Pack, J. D. Special Points for Brillouin-Zone Integrations. Phys. Rev. B 1976, 13, 5188.
references.citation_guidance: Use when Brillouin-zone sampling actually uses a Monkhorst-Pack mesh; generic k-point wording is insufficient.

references.title: Origin of the Overpotential for Oxygen Reduction at a Fuel-Cell Cathode
references.raw_reference: Nørskov, J. K.; Rossmeisl, J.; Logadottir, A.; Lindqvist, L.; Kitchin, J. R.; Bligaard, T.; Jónsson, H. Origin of the Overpotential for Oxygen Reduction at a Fuel Cell Cathode. J. Phys. Chem. B 2004, 108, 17886.
references.citation_guidance: Use when electrochemical free energies actually use the computational hydrogen electrode framework.

references.title: A Python Multiscale Thermochemistry Toolbox (pMuTT) for thermochemical and kinetic parameter estimation
references.raw_reference: Lym, J.; Wittreich, G. R.; Vlachos, D. G. A Python Multiscale Thermochemistry Toolbox (pMuTT) for Thermochemical and Kinetic Parameter Estimation. Comput. Phys. Commun. 2020, 247, 106864.
references.citation_guidance: Use when pMuTT is actually used for thermochemical or kinetic parameter estimation.

references.title: The Atomic Simulation Environment—A Python Library for Working with Atoms
references.raw_reference: Larsen, A. H. et al. The Atomic Simulation Environment—A Python Library for Working with Atoms. J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 2017, 29, 273002.
references.citation_guidance: Use when ASE is actually used to construct, run, or analyze atomistic calculations.

references.title: Structural Relaxation Made Simple
references.raw_reference: Bitzek, E.; Koskinen, P.; Gähler, F.; Moseler, M.; Gumbsch, P. Structural Relaxation Made Simple. Phys. Rev. Lett. 2006, 97, 170201.
references.citation_guidance: Use when the FIRE optimizer is actually used for structural relaxation.

references.title: UMA: A Family of Universal Models for Atoms
references.raw_reference: Wood, B. M. et al. UMA: A Family of Universal Models for Atoms. arXiv:2506.23971 (2025).
